key_insight: A passive nematic can develop periodic and irregular dynamics under steady, spatially varying flow, without velocity fluctuations or hydrodynamic feedback.
engineering_relevance: Steady forcing alone may produce time-dependent nematic responses, complicating the control of liquid-crystal flows.
method: Model a planar passive nematic in prescribed steady Kolmogorov flow.
Use bifurcation and phase-space analyses to track transitions as forcing increases.
Develop two-mode and five-mode reduced-order models.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports stationary-to-periodic-to-irregular transitions, with a two-mode model capturing periodic onset through a saddle-node infinite-period bifurcation and a five-mode model recovering the broader progression.
watch_item: The prescribed-flow model excludes hydrodynamic feedback, so its predictions require validation for fully coupled nematic flows.
paper_title: Complex nematic dynamics driven by steady Kolmogorov flows
